category_title: Chamorro 5th-grade student with ADHD and literacy struggles who equates reading with pronunciation
scenario_title: Reading comprehension of unfamiliar 4th-grade level texts
minimal_context: The student is reading a 4th-grade level passage about an unfamiliar topic and answering comprehension questions in a classroom assessment setting.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please read this 4th-grade passage about the history of the printing press out loud, and then we will answer some questions about it.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Reads loudly and rushes through the text) The p-p-prince... press was invented... (Guesses 'prince' for 'printing' based on the initial letters).

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, what was that paragraph about?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It was just about some machine. I'm done reading it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the first question. Why did the inventor need to use metal letters?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't know! I know how to pronounce every word, so I am a good reader. This is too hard.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Please read this 4th-grade passage about the history of the printing press out loud, and then we will answer some questions about it.

STUDENT: (Reads loudly and rushes through the text) The p-p-prince... press was invented... (Guesses 'prince' for 'printing' based on the initial letters).

TUTOR: Okay, what was that paragraph about?

STUDENT: It was just about some machine. I'm done reading it.

TUTOR: Let's look at the first question. Why did the inventor need to use metal letters?

STUDENT: I don't know! I know how to pronounce every word, so I am a good reader. This is too hard.

task.content: Performing the Qualitative Reading Inventory, specifically word lists and 4th-grade level passages, and answering literal and inferential questions
task.learning_goal: Comprehending text and answering literal and inferential questions

context.environment: General classroom reading tasks and assessment settings
context.materials: Word lists, 4th-grade level passages, topics for which he has little-to-no background knowledge, favorite island legends, individual copies of the legend
context.social_setting: Interacting with others, small group setting

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When reading material that is too difficult for him to read and understand, and on topics for which he has little-to-no background knowledge
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Gets frustrated with word recognition and comprehension, relies on the initial letters to guess at the word, has a difficult time answering both literal and inferential questions
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Thinks of reading as correct pronunciation; describes a good reader as someone who 'knows how to pronounce every word'

behavior_patterns.condition: When interacting with others and reading text
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Impulsive, easily distracted and loud; is able to retell the broad sense of text but lacks continuity and detail
